sources.title: 1860 population census: Spencer Horner household
sources.date: Reference date 1 June 1860; enumeration heading 20 June 1860
sources.provenance: Extracted without alteration from page 1 of the owner-supplied Google Doc export “1860 census,” retrieved 17 October 2026. Heading: Mulberry Township, Johnson County, Arkansas; post office Clarksville. Page No. appears 98, with another handwritten 99; stamped 1029. Dwelling 698, family 699, lines 1–7. NARA series/roll and provider image ID have not been independently reconciled.
sources.supports: Spencer Horner, age 52, farmer, Tennessee; reported real estate $1,500 and personal estate $1,500. Permelia appears on line 2.
sources.limits: Census relationships are not stated in this schedule. Difficult ages and given names require a second reader. Values do not prove cash on hand, total acreage, or an attacker’s motive. Township heading differs from the archive’s earlier Floyd label.
sources.rights: Underlying 1860 federal record; no provider interface is included. Scan provider and reproduction terms still to be recorded.

sources.title: William Riley Horner marker photograph
sources.date: Marker gives death 10 August 1864; photograph date unknown
sources.provenance: Existing repository screenshot of a marker. Photographer, capture date, marker installation date, and reproduction permission have not been established.
sources.supports: The visible inscription attributes the killing to parties known to his family and gives William’s death date as 10 August 1864.
sources.limits: A memorial is evidence of commemoration. It does not name the killers, establish 2 August as the attack date, prove the date it was installed, or establish whether authorities investigated.
sources.rights: Photograph rights unresolved. Link for study; obtain permission or a new authorized photograph before exhibition or classroom image republication.

sources.title: Family narrative attributed to Eva Horner, 1942
sources.provenance: Published repository excerpts and reconstruction refer to FindAGrave memorial 9297073. The earlier website attributes the narrator to Prof. John Turner Horner, “Dad” to his father Dr. John Turner Horner, and recording in 1942 to Eva Horner, the professor’s daughter. This reported second-hand transmission chain and the complete dated manuscript remain unverified. The arranged website excerpt blocks do not establish original manuscript continuity.
sources.supports: The family account describes Spencer being shot after surrendering, William receiving a head wound, and later reprisals.
sources.limits: The reported seventeen-of-twenty reprisal count, names, tactics, hidden money, and exact chronology are uncorroborated here. Excerpt publication is not a complete diplomatic transcript. The reviewer-quoted Jess Wilson sentence does not identify the party or fight; its antecedent remains unresolved. Original transcript unchecked; antecedent of “they” unresolved. The preceding published sentence is “Dad said Jess Wilson was a brave man too.”
sources.rights: Text permission and original custody unresolved. The optional memory extension uses an attributed editorial summary; core assessment does not depend on it.

sources.title: Military and pension research leads
sources.provenance: Earlier archive summaries cited a quotation ('reported killed by guerillas 10 August, 1864, Johnson Co., Arkansas') attributed to a William Riley CMSR card and to a 'Muster roll, August 8, 1865'; the card/roll has not been produced and the 'Reviewed (Fold3)'/tier-Primary designations are withdrawn (F1). The 1867 AG roster (S08) now independently verifies the substance of the service/death claim. WC75885, application 1,143,763, and the Hiram Boen CMSR material remain unretrieved leads.
sources.supports: Identifies records to retrieve and compare; no new authentication of their quoted contents.
sources.limits: WC75885 concerns William Riley’s widow; it is not John Turner’s rejected application. Sturges authorship/date/context/independence remain open. AWOL status does not locate Hiram Boen or implicate him in killings.
sources.rights: Request repository copies and record-level citations before facsimile publication.

sources.title: 1867 Report of the Adjutant General of Arkansas — 2nd and 4th Infantry rosters
sources.path: Internet Archive reportadjutantg01offigoog (remote; no local copy held)
sources.provenance: Report of the Adjutant General of Arkansas, for the Period of the Late Rebellion, and to November 1, 1866 (Government Printing Office, 1867), Internet Archive item reportadjutantg01offigoog (287 scan leaves). Visually inspected 19 October 2026: 2nd Arkansas Infantry roster, printed pp. 205–231 (PDF page N = printed page N-9); 1st Arkansas Infantry roster, pp. 169–204 (no Horner of any name); 4th Arkansas Infantry partial roster (men 'not consolidated'), pp. 233–234. The item's OCR contains zero 'Horner' hits — tables were read from page images, not OCR.
sources.supports: Company K, 2nd Arkansas Infantry (U.S.), printed p. 230–231: Horner, Lewis C. (enl. Feb. 15, 1864, mus. Mar. 8, 1864, mustered out with regiment); Horner, Andrew (enl. Mar. 29, 1864, mus. June 27, 1864, 'Died of measles at Lewisburg, Arkansas, July 31, 1864'); Horner, William R. (enl. Dec. 6, 1863, mus. Feb. 19, 1864, 'Killed by guerillas in Johnson county, Arkansas, August 10, 1864'); Horner, Pleasant (enl. Mar. 29, 1864, mus. June 27, 1864, 'Died of fever at Lewisburg, Arkansas, August 4, 1864'). No John Turner Horner in the 2nd (complete), 1st (complete, officers checked), or 4th (partial) rosters. 4th Infantry, Co. A, Deserted, p. 234: Horner, Andrew ('Deserted at Van Buren, Arkansas, June 8, 1864'; enl. Jan. 12, 1864, mus. Feb. 29, 1864); Horner, Pleasant ('Deserted at Clarksville, Arkansas, May 5, 1864'; enl. April 27, 1864, never mustered).
sources.limits: The roster gives no ages, birthplaces, or physical descriptions — the 2nd-vs-4th Andrew/Pleasant identity question cannot be resolved from it (CMSR jackets required). The 2nd's Andrew prints no middle initial. William's duty/absence status at death is not stated. The 4th roster is explicitly partial (Company A only, no officer listings). Cavalry rosters (pp. 10–168) were not inspected.
sources.rights: Public-domain government publication; Internet Archive scan.
sources.sha256: not-applicable — remote scan, no local copy held
